bull_case: Disciplined N2/A16/packaging investment converts AI demand into sustained high-return capacity.
bear_case: Political diversification could force structurally lower-return capex and dilute the historical Taiwan cluster economics.
thesis: Capital allocation is dominated by organic reinvestment rather than M&A or buybacks. This is appropriate for a foundry where technology leadership and capacity timing determine moat durability. The key question is returns on overseas duplication, not financial engineering.

evidence.claim: FY2025 capex was NT$1.272T and R&D NT$246.4B.
2Q26 margins rose to 67.7% gross and 60.3% operating despite aggressive expansion.

counterevidence: Overseas fabs carry structurally higher costs; customer concentration and Taiwan/export-control tail risks remain material.
unknowns: AI/HPC demand duration beyond the current capacity-constrained cycle
falsifiers: A sustained loss of leading-edge share, repeated yield delays, or owner FCF/share stagnation despite rising capex would weaken the thesis.

hard_veto_flags.veto: 경영진 정직성 또는 회계 신뢰성 훼손
hard_veto_flags.rationale: No restatement, auditor disagreement or management-integrity impairment is established in the frozen 20-F.

key_kpis.name: owner FCF/share
key_kpis.threshold: sustained growth through the capex cycle

next_checks: 3Q26 results, N2 ramp, CoWoS/advanced packaging capacity, overseas-fab margin, top-customer concentration

subscores.rationale: Management consistently funds R&D, leading-edge capacity and packaging ahead of demand while preserving dividends and net cash.
20-F shows effective controls, no restatement flag, long operating record and conservative balance-sheet management.
TSMC has repeatedly delivered node ramps, yield improvement and global capacity expansion while adjusting mix toward HPC/AI.

uncertainties.rationale: AI-cycle duration, overseas economics and geopolitical/customer concentration remain material uncertainties.
